Aditi — great to meet you. Putting initial plan below and tagging Ben/Monica for ops and exec approvals.

Quick answers up front:
- SCIM service-account: we recommend a single dedicated App Service Account per environment (staging/prod). That gives clear audit and scoped credentials. We'll provide a delegation guide.
- IP allowlist: for the dry-run we'll give a 3-entry CIDR suggestion (regional egress). Production allowlist will be more granular; we'll follow Lumenly's IP policy.
- Audit logs: Redwood supplies provisioning events with timestamps, actor (service account or admin), and delta payload. We'll export a CSV slice for your SOC review as part of the dry-run.

Proposed timeline:
1) Sep 18 — scoping call to finalize SA scopes + SCIM attribute mapping (30m)
2) Oct 6 — dry-run (staging) with limited CIDRs
3) Oct 20 — production cutover start; rollover window Oct 20-22 with rollback plan

I'll attach a draft runbook and SA delegation guide after Ben reviews.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick operational notes from the implementation perspective:

1) Service accounts: we'll create two RBAC profiles for the App SA — one for staging (provision-only, limited to user create/update) and one for prod (provision + deprovision, audit-write). Keys will be rotated per your cadence; we can integrate KMS/HSM if required.
2) IP allowlist proposal for dry-run (staging): 3 CIDRs (us-west egress): 52.24.0.0/18, 34.208.0.0/14, 3.101.0.0/16 — these give stable coverage for our staging pool. If Lumenly uses strict egress NATs we can tighten.
3) Rollback: we will maintain a one-click fallback to previous auth config for 4 hours post-cutover in case of provisioning regressions.

Ask: Aditi — can you confirm who on your side will test user provisioning (name + email) during the dry-run and who has authority to approve the prod cutover? We need two approvers.

Ben Carter
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
